title: Grateful Dead Live at Roscoe Maples Pavilion, Stanford U. on 1973-02-09
lineage: SBD> MR> REEL> DAT> SS> CDR> DAW (Bertha)> CDA

ai_review.summary: A superb soundboard remix of the historic Feb 9 1973 show brims with first‑time classics – Eyes, Here Comes Sunshine, Row Jimmy and more – captured in surprisingly clear audio.
ai_review.review: This recording (a Jay Ashley “Bertha” sound‑board source) has been remixed to tame the original’s rough, crunchy edge, delivering a clean enough mix that lets the band’s historic energy shine through. The concert is celebrated for its avalanche of debut performances – Eyes of the World, Here Comes Sunshine, Row Jimmy, China Doll, Loose Lucy and others – all delivered with high‑octane playing and memorable jams (Truckin’→Eyes→China Doll). While a few listeners note occasional pitch drift or bitey highs, the overall listening experience is overwhelmingly positive.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 80 reviews, most 4‑5 stars; show praised for historic first‑time songs and high energy (70% weight), recording described as rough but significantly improved by remix (30% weight).

recording_quality.technical_notes: Original board was "rough and ready"/crunchy with occasional pitch or bite issues; the Ashley remix cleans up clarity, balances levels and makes the performance enjoyable despite minor artifacts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A landmark set packed with debut material; first‑time songs flow seamlessly, especially the high‑energy Truckin’→Eyes→China Doll segue. The second set builds intensity and keeps a lively momentum throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar tone is described as crunchy yet true to live sound; many note his standout playing on new songs.
